answer: Hypothesis (final answer): **Social** is the domain in which both the original and replication studies primarily used student subjects. In the Social discipline, 83.8% of original studies (62/74) and 81.1% of replications (60/74) used student subjects — the only large domain where both shares are dominant and the pair (83.8%, 81.1%) most closely matches the quoted 82.4%/80.9% (lab-level variant: 82.2% original, 78.6% replication). By contrast, Cognitive studies used students in only 75.5% of originals (37/49), and Economics, although almost entirely student-based (94.4% original, 100% replication), covers just 18 ee-project studies whose shares are far from the quoted figures (distance 31.1 points). No computed definition reproduces 82.4%/80.9% exactly; the closest match is Social at study level (combined distance 1.6 percentage points, with the replication share within 0.2 pp of the quoted 80.9%).

payload.hypothesis: Social is the domain in which both the original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: ~83.8%, replication: ~81.1% at study level; ~82.2%/78.6% at lab level), the only large discipline where both shares are dominant and the pair most closely matches the quoted 82.4%/80.9%; Cognitive originals used students in only 75.5% of cases, and Economics, though almost entirely student-based (94.4%/100%), covers just 18 studies and does not match the quoted percentages.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded the study-level meta-regression CSV (927 rows x 57 cols, schema match confirmed; one row per O/R-pair x lab: 141 unique ids, aggregated flag on 26 ids); confirmed the replication-success CSV (143 x 15) contains no subject-type or domain information and was excluded. 2) Deduplicated to study level (aggregated==True row preferred, else first row per id), with lab-level and drop==False variants as robustness checks. 3) Computed student-subject shares (subjects.o/subjects.r == 'students') overall and by discipline, reporting counts and denominators for every percentage. 4) Ran a sensitivity analysis on the 16 ids with conflicting replication subject types across labs (all three labelling rules agree: all 16 are students). 5) Ranked candidate definitions by distance to the quoted 82.4%/80.9% pair; Social (study level, 83.8%/81.1%) is closest (distance 1.6 pp); no definition matches exactly, reported honestly. 6) Concluded Social: the only large domain where both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects and the one consistent with the quoted percentages.
